DocMorris AG
does not primarily sell or manufacture wearable medical devices
, though it distributes routine diabetes self-management supplies and digital health integration tools through partnerships (such as with Roche Diabetes Care)

The
Zur Rose Group
does not manufacture or sell continuous glucose monitors, smartwatches, wearable ECGs, sleep trackers, or remote patient monitoring hardware
. Instead, Zur Rose is a digital pharmacy and e-health service provider that operates online pharmacies and digital medicine platforms in Europe, notably offering medication management via the
Zur Rose App
Context of Digital Health and Wearables
While Zur Rose focuses on prescription and pharmacy services (and previously acquired telehealth provider TeleClinic), remote monitoring devices fall under entirely different technology categories:
PharmiWeb.com
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Invasive or minimally invasive arm or abdomen sensors (such as FreeStyle Libre or Dexcom) tracking interstitial fluid sugar levels.
Amazon.in
Smartwatches & Wearables:
Wrist-based devices with PPG and electrical sensors used for general fitness, sleep quality evaluation, and occasional single-lead ECG recordings (like the Apple Watch).
Amazon.in
Regulatory Warning:
Public health agencies like the FDA explicitly warn consumers against relying on commercial smartwatches or smart rings that claim to perform non-invasive blood glucose measurements, as they lack clinical clearance and risk dangerous dosing errors.
